Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{6},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{5\pi }{12}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Which of the following could be the image of the top side of $Δ$ under the action of $T?$

choices.value: The image is the empty set

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14047173/assets/0963fc3c56b5baac68e2d587896bf4655950640ecce5b924edc2d8e26a3e64e2.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{4}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

The image of the bottom side of $Δ$ under the action of $T$ is a line segment. Which of the following statements are true regarding the image?

- The image makes the angle of $0$ with the positive $x$-axis.
- The image makes the angle of $\frac{\pi }{4}$ with the positive $x$-axis.
- One endpoint of the image is the origin $O$ of the $xy$-plane, and the other endpoint lies on the circle of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at $O.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the bottom side.

For the bottom side, we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le \sqrt{3}.$ 

Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =(u,\,0),\,0\le u\le \sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a parametric equation of the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14047173/assets/92bd315a07a5d76e77c249c12ea4544ee1555b0c214c68cf1f92fc3f07a71ddf.png)

 

Note that the line that this segment lies on passes through the origin. 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. The slope of the line is

$$
k=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0}{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}=\operatorname{tan}⁡0.
$$

As a result, our line makes an angle of $0$ radians with the positive $x$-axis.

- Statement III is true.

- When $u=0,$ we obtain the point 
$(0,\,0),$
which is the origin $O$ of the $xy$-plane.

- When $u=\sqrt{3},$ we obtain the point 
$(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡0),$
whose distance to $O$ is $\sqrt{3}.$

So, one endpoint of the segment is the origin $O$ of the $xy$-plane, while the other endpoint lies on the circle with radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at $O.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
